skills.name: Establish subtraction-ready representation
skills.definition: Prepare quantities so subtraction can proceed by rewriting numbers into compatible forms, including finding a common denominator for fractional parts and normalizing whole or mixed numbers into subtraction-ready form.
skills.merge_rationale: S01 and S02 are both preparatory setup skills that occur before core subtraction. In the dossiers, both serve the same problem-solving phase: making the operands compatible for subtraction. They are distinct at fine grain, but at K=5 they can be merged without losing the major diagnostic distinction between setup, subtraction, regrouping, and finishing.

skills.name: Subtract aligned parts
skills.definition: Carry out subtraction once quantities are in compatible form, including subtracting numerators over a common denominator and subtracting whole-number parts of mixed numbers.
skills.merge_rationale: Kept separate because this is the core execution step and has strong independent diagnostic value. Students may prepare correctly yet still make arithmetic or alignment errors here.

skills.name: Borrow across parts
skills.definition: Regroup one whole as fractional units and adjust the whole-number part when direct subtraction of fractional parts would produce a negative result.
skills.merge_rationale: Kept separate because borrowing/regrouping produces a distinctive error pattern and does not occur in all items. It remains diagnostically important to distinguish from ordinary subtraction.

skills.name: Simplify result
skills.definition: Reduce the computed result to lowest terms or eliminate a zero fractional part after subtraction.
skills.merge_rationale: Kept separate because simplification is a post-subtraction operation with its own common error patterns, such as failing to reduce or mishandling zero fractional parts.

skills.name: Compose final form
skills.definition: Express the completed result in an appropriate final form, such as a mixed number, fraction, or integer, by combining whole and fractional parts when needed.
skills.merge_rationale: Kept separate because final presentation is conceptually different from simplification: a student may compute and simplify correctly but still fail to express the answer in the proper form.

skills.name: Prepare numbers for subtraction
skills.definition: Rewrite quantities into compatible subtraction-ready forms, including normalizing whole or mixed numbers and creating common denominators for fractional parts when needed.
skills.merge_rationale: This continues the K=5 merge because both skills belong to the same preparation phase and often function as prerequisite setup before any subtraction can occur.

skills.name: Subtract and regroup aligned parts
skills.definition: Perform subtraction on compatible whole and fractional parts, including borrowing/regrouping across whole and fractional parts when direct subtraction would otherwise produce a negative fractional result.
skills.merge_rationale: At this coarser level, S04 is best merged with S03 because borrowing is not a separate phase so much as a conditional extension of subtraction execution. In the dossiers, regrouping appears only in the course of carrying out subtraction of aligned parts, making this a meaningful execution-level aggregate.

skills.name: Simplify result
skills.definition: Reduce the computed result to lowest terms or remove zero fractional parts after subtraction.
skills.merge_rationale: Kept separate because simplification remains a distinct post-computation operation with clear diagnostic value even at a coarser grain.

skills.name: Present final answer form
skills.definition: Combine whole and fractional parts as needed and express the answer in an appropriate final form such as a mixed number, fraction, or integer.
skills.merge_rationale: Kept separate because final answer composition is still distinguishable from simplification: some items require recombination or formatting even when no reduction is needed.

aggregation_notes: The main aggregation logic follows natural phases of fraction-subtraction problem solving visible in the dossiers: preparation, execution, regrouping when needed, simplification, and final presentation. For K=5, the strongest merge is S01 with S02 because both are setup operations that make numbers subtraction-ready. Other skills are preserved because they represent distinct error points. For K=4, S03 and S04 are merged into a broader execution skill since borrowing is a conditional part of carrying out subtraction rather than a fully separate phase at this coarser level. S05 and S06 are not merged because simplification and final formatting can come apart diagnostically: students may simplify incorrectly yet present the form correctly, or vice versa.
